brief: GS's morning note runs five topics. On the Fed, chief economist Mericle argues October is not live: dovish Fedspeak from Daly and Warsh after a firmer CPI print signals the FOMC sticks to a skip-October, hike-in-December plan, with December expected to be the last hike before cuts resume once inflation nears 2% in the back half of 2027; GS's own rate view stays more dovish than market pricing, which keeps funds above 4.5% for years. Treasury trading (Brown) and FX strategy (Cahill) flag the market still pricing meaningful December-hike odds despite coordinated dovish messaging and a Waller-led walkback of October pricing. In credit, Lynam and Shelofsky describe equities near highs while AI-exposed credit (hyperscaler and data-center bonds, USD HY AI project finance) trades near all-time wides on unresolved AI capex funding-cost questions, even as GS calls the recent cheapening a constructive year-end setup, with concentration-risk discounts seen widening further into 2027. On Hungary, Daly expects the deficit to fall to 5% next year, implying euro adoption around January 2031; recent fiscal signals already lifted HUF. On semis, GS attributes part of the CXMT-driven memory selloff to unrelated credit/CPI jitters, arguing a real but narrower-than-priced technology gap remains and valuations overprice a 2028 downcycle. Section five previews the week's data and earnings.
